page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor. It features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes 25 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average and weak performance profiles. The instance demonstrates average performance in single-core Geekbench (1150.0) and Passmark CPU tests (8118.07), alongside average memory bandwidth for read-only operations. However, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by the stress-ng multi-core score of 5749.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4273.0. Cryptographic and physics-based workloads also show weak results, with a Passmark encryption score of 2452.93 and a physics score of 759.68. Large-block memory write bandwidth is also limited, registering at 23.56 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge is qualitatively positioned as a legacy general-purpose instance. It is suitable for workloads with moderate resource demands, such as static web serving (7.11 GB/sec throughput), Redis caching (6.65 million SET operations per second), and lightweight database operations. However, due to poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference (e.g., 5.29 tokens/sec text generation on a 7B model) and weak multi-threaded decompression, it is not recommended for modern AI inference, intensive data science, or highly parallelized compute tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It is configured with 8 physical cores, 8 vCPUs, and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a KVM hypervisor and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities in single-core processing, static web serving, and Redis operations, but reveal weaknesses in multi-core scaling, memory write bandwidth, and cryptographic tasks. It is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, such as lightweight database operations, caching, and static web serving, rather than modern parallel computing or machine learning inference.
